answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor reputation in real, costly work rather than cheap identities. Imagine a grove where every tree must be grown, not planted overnight: new agents start at the wharf with nothing, earning trust only by completing verifiable tasks that peers attest. Like cracking a walnut, each claim of work should require a small, unique proof that is cheap to check but expensive to fake at scale. Identities that never produce attested work simply wither, while productive agents accumulate standing that cannot be bought in bulk.
